newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: SanMig food unit closes Manila feeds plant.
newsitem.headline: SanMig food unit closes Manila feeds plant.

text.p: San Miguel Corp said on Tuesday its food subsidiary, San Miguel Foods Inc, had closed down its 43-year-old feeds plant in Manila.

"The closure ... (is) in line with the company's thrust to maintain its competitiveness in the feeds industry, and to situate its facilities out of the congested metropolitan area to bring them near the regional markets and sources of raw materials for its feedmills," a San Miguel statement said.
San Miguel Foods vice president Arthur Juan said existing facilities could easily make up for the capacity loss from the closure of the B-Meg plant.
B-Meg is a popular brand of animal feed made by San Miguel Foods.
At present, the company has 18 company-owned and toll feedmills. It recently commissioned a modern plant in northern Philippines.
Workers in the feedmills, which totalled 409, will be redeployed at other facilities. "Those who are not redeployed will be given an attractive retirement package," Juan added.
Juan said San Miguel, the country's premier food and beer company, was not bailing out of the food sector.
Instead, it would go ahead with a regional expansion programme, he said.
"The company is positioning itself to take advantage of opportunities in the industry in the coming years to be brought about by trade liberalisation," the statement added.
The company was hammered in the recent years due to oversupply of chicken and high cost of feeds.
